content_metadata.description: A video explaining and demonstrating the flame test which is used to identify metal ions based on the colors they produce when heated.

qAndA.question: What color does the flame turn when testing for potassium ions?

qAndA.answer: They absorb energy and get excited to a higher energy level (absorption process). Then, they fall back to their original energy level, releasing the energy as light (emission process).
qAndA.question: What happens to electrons in the metal ion when heated in the Bunsen burner flame?

qAndA.answer: Because the energy released as light during the emission process is different for each metal ion due to varying electron transitions.
qAndA.question: Why does the flame turn different colors for different metal ions?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: This video is going to be about the flame test to identify the metoion.
A flame test is an analytical procedure used in chemistry to detect the presence of certain
elements, primary metoion, based on each element's characteristic emission spectrum.
The flame tests are most useful for some metals than others. It is very useful for group 1
metals. This flame test provides a good way of quickly identifying the metoion present.
And these are some color of the metoion.
The color originates from the movement of electrons in the metoion. When heated,
electron gets energy and they are excited into higher energy level.
And this is called the absorption process. As electrons are more energetic,
they are unstable, so they tend to fall back to the lower energy level. When they do that,
they release energy as light. And this light has a characteristic flame colors of different
metoion due to varying electron transitions. This is the emission process.
Flame tests is relatively quick and simple. We can do this quite quickly in laboratory.
All you need is the Bunsen burner, some cotton stick, and of course the test sample.
